title: Mocks, Stubs, Fakes & Property-Based Testing
objectives: Distinguish stubs, mocks, fakes and spies
Prefer fakes at real boundaries; assert behavior, not calls
Use property-based tests for algorithmic invariants

examples.name: fake_repo.rs

exercise.prompt: Pick the right double: "canned HTTP 500 response", "in-memory SQLite for repo tests", "assert email service was called", "record calls to inspect later".
hints: Fakes run real-ish logic; stubs just return data.
Mocks verify interactions without return values.

questions.prompt: Why prefer a fake over a mock for a repository in tests?
options: fakes exercise real logic and fail on real conflicts
questions.explanation: A fake keeps behavior (uniqueness, ordering) while dropping I/O; a mock only replays assumptions.

questions.prompt: A good property-based test for encode/decode is…
options: decode never panics on valid input only
questions.explanation: Round-trip invariants are the canonical property: the framework generates many x and shrinks failures.
